rfi.title: PSG celebrations marred by violence as French authorities report 890 arrests
rfi.description: French authorities have arrested over 890 people after outbreaks of violence followed Paris Saint-Germain’s Champions League victory on Saturday, as the government defended its policing operation amid sharp criticism from the right.

rfi.title: France boards fourth Russian oil tanker as crackdown on ‘shadow fleet’ continues
rfi.description: The French Navy has boarded another oil tanker from Russia as Paris steps up its campaign against Moscow’s so-called "shadow fleet" of vessels suspected of evading international sanctions.

rfi.title: France weighs tougher safeguards against child abuse in schools
rfi.description: French lawmakers will on Monday debate tougher protections against sexual abuse in schools and after-school programmes, as a series of scandals increases pressure on the government to strengthen safeguards.

rfi.title: Last hurrah:  Algeria's Riyad Mahrez
rfi.description: Riyad Mahrez will play for Algeria for the second time at the World Cup at the age of 35. In the fourth instalment of a series on players at their final World Cup, RFI looks at the career of a striker who has risen from modest clubs to international stardom.

rfi.title: First contact: Curaçao’s rise to the global stage
rfi.description: Curaçao will make its World Cup debut at the 2026 tournament in the United States, Mexico and Canada. In the first instalment of a four-part series, RFI looks at the journey of the smallest nation to qualify for the competition in its 96-year history.

rfi.title: Football heroes: PSG victory toasted by thousands of fans in Paris
rfi.description: The French capital held a hero's welcome for Paris Saint-Germain players who won their second consecutive Champions League title with celebrations under heavy security after a night of revelry marred by unrest. The team was received by President Emmanuel Macron ahead of a victory parade which drew thousands of supporters.

rfi.title: France requests emergency UN meeting amid Israeli advance in Lebanon
rfi.description: France has requested an emergency meeting of the United Nations Security Council after Israeli forces seized the medieval Beaufort castle in Lebanon, the French foreign minister said Sunday.

rfi.title: Ethiopia election overshadowed by war, instability and muted opposition
rfi.description: Ethiopia goes to the polls on Monday in an election which is expected to return Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed’s Prosperity Party to power, but has been marked by instability, restricted voting and questions over whether the vote can challenge the status quo.

rfi.title: Hundreds detained after violent clashes on PSG victory night
rfi.description: More than 700 people on Saturday were detained across France, over 200 in Paris alone, after violent clashes erupted when thousands poured onto the streets after Paris Saint-Germain's Champions League final victory against English club Arsenal.

rfi.title: Last hurrah: Brazil's Neymar
rfi.description: Neymar will play for Brazil at the World Cup for the fourth time at the age of 34. In the third of a series on players at their final World Cup, RFI looks back at the career of a striker who holds his country's record for both scoring and assisting goals.

rfi.title: Japan's SoftBank to spend €75bn on AI centres in France
rfi.description: Japanese tech investor SoftBank will spend €75 billion ($87.5 billion) on artificial intelligence infrastructure in France, its founder Masayoshi Son told a French newspaper in an interview published Saturday.

rfi.title: Women gain ground in France as running clubs turn sport into community
rfi.description: Statistics show that most people now taking up running in France are women. In Paris, some run alone and some in running groups – which are booming in the French capital as women turn to them for motivation, safety and a sense of community.

rfi.title: 'We are here to help': WHO chief visits epicentre of Ebola outbreak in DR Congo
rfi.description: UN health chief Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus on Saturday visited Bunia in the eastern Democratic Republic of Congo - where a severe Ebola outbreak has been declared.

rfi.title: Cinema should be 'a place for everyone': Cannes rising star Anna Cazenave Cambet
rfi.description: French director Anna Cazenave Cambet first came to Cannes in 2016 as a student with a short film called Gabber Lover, which won the Queer Palm award. With two feature films under her belt, she returned to the Croisette in 2026 as one of the "10 to Watch" rising French stars. RFI spoke to her about finding her place as a young woman in the industry, and her hopes for the future of cinema.

rfi.title: Can the French cinema industry take on its biggest financial backer?
rfi.description: French cinema is reeling after the CEO of the country's biggest investor in films, Canal+, said he would no longer work with hundreds of actors, directors, producers and technicians who signed an open letter criticising the right-wing views of media mogul Vincent Bolloré, who owns a 30 percent share of the company. But given the number of signatories, can Maxime Saada follow through on his threat?

rfi.title: French singer Patrick Bruel cancels slew of concerts amid rape allegations
rfi.description: Facing mounting allegations of rape and assault, popular French singer and actor Patrick Bruel announced on Friday the cancellation of all his concerts until the fall, including dates in Paris and festivals. He is not expected to return to the stage to perform before October.

rfi.title: Turkey enters political unknown after police raid opposition party headquarters
rfi.description: Turkey's main opposition CHP was thrown into fresh disarray Saturday as court-installed leader Kemal Kilicdaroglu made his first visit to party headquarters since a controversial court ruling scrapped a 2023 party primary. Ozgur Ozel, the CHP leader ousted by the decision, called for an urgent congress, telling thousands at an Ankara rally that the party "cannot be run by an appointed leader".

rfi.title: Last hurrah: Senegal's Sadio Mané
rfi.description: Sadio Mané will play for Senegal at the World Cup for a second time at the age of 34. In the second of a series on players at their final World Cup, RFI looks at a striker who holds his country's goal-scoring record.

euronews.description: The budget airline's stock rose more than 12% after Castlelake said it was considering a possible offer. euronews.description: Global health body CEPI is fast-tracking three experimental vaccines against the Bundibugyo strain of Ebola as the outbreak in Central Africa continues to spread.

euronews.description: The EU is set to approve its controversial migration law, allowing return hubs outside the bloc, extending detention periods and introducing measures aimed at accelerating deportations – reflecting growing voter fears over migration.

euronews.description: Participants with the family name of O'Sullivan and Sullivan broke the world record this weekend for the largest gathering of people with the same surname, in County Cork, Ireland.

euronews.title: Higher airfares and fewer visitors: How the Iran conflict is hitting Southeast Asia tourism
euronews.description: Tourism across Southeast Asia was finally recovering from the pandemic. Now, soaring fuel prices, flight disruptions, and growing economic uncertainty linked to the Iran conflict are threatening to slow demand just as the region enters its crucial summer travel season.

euronews.description: Austrian law provides for the jurisdiction of local courts over certain offences committed abroad and the Vienna court has jurisdiction in this case because the defendants reside there.

euronews.description: Germany generated more electricity from solar and wind in 2025 than any other EU country – but its prices remain tied to volatile fossil fuels.

lemonde.title: La Coupe du monde 2026, un défi sécuritaire titanesque pour les forces de l’ordre américaines

lemonde.title: EN DIRECT, Roland-Garros 2026 : Anna Kalinskaya se qualifie pour les quarts, Flavio Cobolli à un jeu du match face à Zachary Svajda

lemonde.title: André Santini, maire d’Issy-les-Moulineaux et ancien député UDI, est mort à l’âge de 85 ans
lemonde.description: Pendant son demi-siècle de mandat, il avait transformé l’ancienne ville ouvrière des Hauts-de-Seine en un « médialand », accueillant les sièges de nombreux médias. La fin de son carrière avait été marquée par des accusations de harcèlement sexuel et moral. Il s’est éteint dans la nuit de dimanche à lundi à l’âge de 85 ans.

lemonde.title: « L’habitabilité est la condition de tous nos droits et libertés » : l’entretien avec le philosophe Baptiste Morizot et le juriste Laurent Neyret
lemonde.description: Dans un court essai, ils estiment que le droit de l’environnement plie souvent devant d’autres traditions juridiques plus solidement fondées, et proposent d’appeler « habitabilité » la valeur que ce droit est appelé à protéger.

lemonde.title: Pourquoi la hausse des indemnités des arrêts de travail ne s’explique pas par les « abus »

Les chercheurs soulignent plutôt la dégradation des conditions de travail et le recul de l’âge de départ à la retraite.

france24fr.title: Tchad : l'Oasis de Bachikélé, un point d'eau vital et préservé pour les nomades du Sahara
france24fr.description: Nichée au cœur des montagnes rouges du Sahara tchadien, l'Oasis de Bachikélé s'impose comme un site exceptionnel et un point de ravitaillement hautement stratégique pour les caravanes nomades. Relativement épargnée par les sécheresses récurrentes qui frappent la région, cette source pérenne dissimulée au milieu des étendues de sable offre bien plus qu’un simple paysage spectaculaire : elle constitue un abri et un havre de paix indispensable à la survie locale.

france24fr.title: Madagascar : quatre juges constitutionnels visés par des poursuites pour "complot"
france24fr.description: À Madagascar, le parquet d'Antananarivo a ouvert une procédure pénale pour « complot en vue de déstabilisation » visant quatre magistrats de la Haute Cour constitutionnelle (HCC). Cette offensive judiciaire a été déclenchée au lendemain d'une décision cruciale rendue par la HCC concernant une demande de destitution du président de la Refondation, le colonel Michaël Randrianirina.

france24fr.title: Kenya : huit arrestations après l'incendie mortel dans un dortoir de filles
france24fr.description: Au Kenya, huit élèves ont été arrêtées par la police, soupçonnées d'être impliquées dans l'incendie criminel qui a ravagé un dortoir de l'Utumishi Girls Academy jeudi dernier. Ce drame a coûté la vie à 16 étudiantes et fait près de 80 blessées, alors que les familles attendent toujours de pouvoir identifier les corps des victimes.

france24fr.title: Flotte fantôme russe : un quatrième pétrolier arraisonné par la Marine française en Atlantique
france24fr.description: Soutenue par le Royaume-Uni, la Marine française a intercepté au large de la Bretagne le Tagor, un navire russe sous sanctions naviguant sous un faux pavillon. C'est le quatrième bâtiment de la flotte fantôme de Moscou immobilisé par la France depuis septembre dernier. Dénonçant le contournement des sanctions qui financent la guerre en Ukraine, Emmanuel Macron a affiché sa fermeté alors que Paris annonce vouloir doubler les amendes.

france24fr.title: Entre le Liban, Gaza et la Cisjordanie, Israël impose un remodelage territorial par la force
france24fr.description: De la Cisjordanie au Liban en passant par Gaza, Israël mène une refonte territoriale majeure par la politique du fait accompli. Cette stratégie globale s'illustre par l'annexion hautement symbolique du château de Beaufort au Sud-Liban, des frappes continues à Gaza pour en contrôler 70 %, et le lancement officiel du projet de colonisation E1 qui fracture définitivement la Cisjordanie. En agissant simultanément sur tous ces fronts, le gouvernement israélien verrouille sa domination et redessine du

france24fr.title: Guinée, des élections législatives et communales marquées par une faible participation
france24fr.description:
En Guinée, près de 7 millions d'électeurs étaient appelés aux urnes ce dimanche pour les élections législatives et communales.
 
Une étape importante dans le rétablissement de l'ordre constitutionnel, cinq ans après le coup d'Etat de 2021 qui avait porté Mamadi Doumbouya au pouvoir.
 
De leur côté, plusieurs partis politiques d'opposition avaient appelé au boycott du scrutin.

france24fr.title: Flotte fantôme russe : un nouveau pétrolier arraisonné par la France
france24fr.description: La Marine française a arraisonné dimanche un nouveau pétrolier en provenance de Russie, lors d'une opération menée en haute mer dans l'Atlantique "avec le soutien de plusieurs partenaires, dont le Royaume-Uni", a annoncé lundi Emmanuel Macron.

france24fr.title: Erdogan : plus puissant que jamais ? Parlons-en avec Ayşegül Sert, Didier Billion et Samim Akgönül
france24fr.description: En Turquie, l’offensive du pouvoir contre l’opposition semble être passée sous les radars médiatiques. Pourtant, un an après l’arrestation du maire d’Istanbul Ekrem Imamoglu, jamais Recep Tayyip Erdogan n’était allé si loin, semble-t-il, pour assoir sa mainmise sur le pays en écartant le chef désigné du CHP, Özgür Özel. Existe-t-il encore une possibilité d’exister pour l’opposition démocratique turque ?

france24fr.title: Faux comptes, fausse Pride… l'Arménie face à une désinformation tous azimuts avant les élections
france24fr.description: Les médias d’investigation arméniens ont démasqué de nombreuses campagnes de désinformation en ligne depuis le début du mois de mai, à l’approche des élections législatives du 7 juin. Parti au pouvoir, opposition et acteurs étrangers sont tous accusés d'en être à l'origine, malgré les risques pour la démocratie arménienne.

france24fr.title: Colombie : l'ultra-conservateur Abelardo de la Espriella crée la surprise et accède au second tour
france24fr.description: L'ultra-conservateur Abelardo de la Espriella, surnommé « le Tigre », a déjoué les pronostics en se qualifiant pour le second tour de la présidentielle face à Ivan Cepeda, le candidat de la gauche sortante. Alors que l'outsider de droite promet une guerre totale contre les cartels et des méga-prisons, son rival dénonce des irrégularités ainsi que des ingérences étrangères, exigeant un recomptage des voix avant le scrutin du 21 juin.

france24fr.title: Les débordements autour de la victoire du PSG à Paris, un terrain politique
france24fr.description: Le ministre de l'Intérieur a fait état d'un bilan de plus de 890 arrestations et 178 forces de l'ordre blessées lors des festivités du week-end, une hausse de 45 % par rapport à 2025. Malgré ces violences, le gouvernement défend sa gestion de la sécurité tandis que les vives réactions de l'opposition confirment une nouvelle fois que le football reste un terrain hautement politique. Une loi serait en préparation pour condamner les casseurs lors de ce genre d'événements et compliquer l'achat de ma

france24fr.title: Moyen-Orient : le Koweït de nouveau visé par des attaques de missiles et de drones
france24fr.description: Pour la deuxième fois en moins d'une semaine, le Koweït a été la cible de frappes de missiles et de drones menées par Téhéran contre une base militaire américaine. Cette escalade, marquée par des tirs croisés entre Washington et l'Iran ce week-end, fragilise grandement les négociations en cours autour d'une nouvelle proposition d'accord et de cessez-le-feu de Donald Trump.

france24fr.title: Ebola : que peut l'IA face aux épidémies ?
france24fr.description: L’épidémie d’Ebola en République démocratique du Congo “progresse plus vite que nous”, s’est alarmé le chef de l’Organisation mondiale de la santé, Si aucun traitement ni vaccin n’est disponible face à la souche actuellement en circulation - Bundibugyo, une nouvelle arme pourrait sauver des vies : il s’agit de l’intelligence artificielle. Explications de Sophian Aubin dans le “rendez-vous Afrique” de France 24.

france24fr.title: Ethiopie : Addis-Abeba se métamorphose... Une modernisation à marche forcée
france24fr.description: En Ethiopie, 50 millions d'électeurs sont appelés aux urnes ce lundi pour les législatives. Le scrutin s’annonce sans suspense, le Parti de la Prospérité (PP) du Premier ministre sortant Abiy Ahmed, candidat à sa propre succession, fait figure de favori. Au pouvoir depuis 2018, Abiy Ahmed est critiqué pour son autoritarisme et sa répression des voix dissidentes. Lui vante son bilan et son "projet corridor". Il compte transformer l'Ethiopie en "Dubaï de l'Afrique". Depuis 2024, Addis-Abeba et d'a

france24fr.title: Gaza : l'extension du contrôle israélien menace un cessez-le-feu déjà fragile
france24fr.description: En violation flagrante du cessez-le-feu conclu en octobre 2025, Benjamin Netanyahu a ordonné à son armée d'étendre son contrôle à 70% de la bande de Gaza, aggravant une situation déjà marquée par les tueries et la famine. Deux frappes ont fait plusieurs morts et des dizaines de blessés ce week-end.

france24fr.title: Cisjordanie : Israël s'apprête à lancer les travaux du projet de colonie E1
france24fr.description: Le projet de colonisation E1, qui tient particulièrement à cœur au gouvernement israélien, entre dans sa phase active avec le lancement des appels d'offres, comme l'explique le journaliste de France 24 Stéphane Amar. Ce plan de construction vise à relier Jérusalem à la colonie de Ma'ale Adumim. france24fr.title: Violences à l'école en France : les députés se penchent sur la proposition de loi post-Bétharram
france24fr.description: Les députés examinent lundi 1er juin la proposition de loi visant à lutter contre les violences exercées sur les enfants à l'école et dans le périscolaire, rédigée dans le sillage de l'enquête parlementaire ouverte après le scandale de Bétharram

zeit.description: Der AfD-Landesverband Niedersachsen darf laut einem Gericht als sogenanntes Beobachtungsobjekt von erheblicher Bedeutung behandelt werden. Einen Eilantrag wies es ab.

Benjamin Netanjahu: Generalstaatsanwältin sieht Demokratie unter Netanjahu gefährdet
zeit.description: Angesichts der innenpolitischen Situation in Israel zeigt sich die Generalstaatsanwältin besorgt. Sie warnt unter anderem vor Angriffen auf die Justiz des Landes.

zeit.title: Rentenversicherung: Beitrag zur Rentenversicherung könnte 2028 auf fast 20 Prozent steigen
zeit.description: 2027 soll der Beitragssatz zur Rente noch stabil bleiben, im Jahr darauf droht laut Berechnungen ein Plus von 1,3 Punkten. Das wäre etwas mehr als bislang angenommen.

zeit.title: Syrien: In Syrien inhaftierte Journalistin ist in »schlechter« Verfassung
zeit.description: Die in Syrien inhaftierte deutsche Journalistin Eva-Maria Michelmann befindet sich in einem »schlechten« Zustand. Ihrem Anwalt zufolge sei sie »deutlich abgemagert«.

zeit.title: Eizellspende: Mit den Eizellen einer 19-Jährigen
zeit.description: Sie war Mitte 40, wollte unbedingt mehr Kinder, aber es klappte nicht. Also ließ sie sich die Eizellen spenden. In Dänemark. Sollte das auch in Deutschland erlaubt sein?

zeit.title: Elektroauto: Öl wechseln muss man nicht, aber die Rechnung ist trotzdem höher
zeit.description: Von Elektroautos erhoffen sich viele Kunden niedrige Kosten im Unterhalt. Allerdings zeigen erste Erfahrungen, dass Werkstätten eigene Ideen zur Instandhaltung haben.

observador.title: Nos EUA, dizem que o Pentágono quer "drones assassinos ba...
observador.description: Uma reportagem do Washington Post aponta para uma corrida ao que descreve como "bombas voadoras baratas" e até já há uma competição para isso. Ainda, iranianos de olho no mercado imobiliário.

observador.title: As notícias das 13h
observador.description: As notícias na Rádio Observador. Aconteça o que acontecer.

observador.title: Coimbra. Plataforma de TVDE com operação 100% elétrica
observador.description: A operar por agora apenas em Coimbra, a plataforma TAPSi conta com mais de cinco mil utilizadores registados e mais de 200 motoristas associados, apostando numa remuneração mais justa.

observador.title: Princesa norueguesa perseguida na Austrália
observador.description: Uma "carta suspeita" foi intercetada pelos seguranças da família real e uma ordem de restrição foi emitida contra o suspeito. Ingrid Alexandra deve regressar "em breve" à Noruega, disse Haakon.

observador.title: Dívida pública aumenta para 287,1 mil milhões de euros
observador.description: Variação "refletiu, sobretudo, o aumento dos títulos de dívida (+3,5 mil milhões de euros), distribuído entre curto prazo (+2,5 mil milhões de euros) e longo prazo (+1,0 mil milhões de euros)".

observador.title: Preço das casas alto: há risco na capacidade de pagar
observador.description: Com o aumento dos preços da habitação e dos custos de construção, o desequilíbrio entre oferta e procura deverá persistir: as medidas do Governo "estimularam ainda mais o mercado", avança a DBRS.

observador.title: Greve. Metro do Porto mantém em funcionamento duas linhas
observador.description: Metro "funcionará durante o dia na Linha Amarela", bem como "entre a Sra. da Hora e o Dragão", com frequências de passagem de 15 minutos entre as 7h e as 20h, e de 30 minutos entre as 6h e as 7h.

observador.title: Em estreia esta semana: 8 séries, 2 documentários e Bardem
observador.description: Há trabalho novo de Mindy Kaling, há detalhes do julgamento de Michael Jackson, há histórias do futebol para recordar. Mas a estreia mais esperada é a de "Cape Fear", na Apple TV+.

observador.title: O que explica as críticas à Prestação Social Única? — Debate
observador.description: O Governo vai substituir 13 apoios pela Prestação Social Única e admite condicionar o acesso através de um sistema. A medida divide opiniões, principalmente com críticas dos partidos à esquerda.

observador.title: OMS e RDCongo desenvolvem vacina contra Ébola
observador.description: Governo e a OMS têm insistido para que as comunidades adotem "comportamentos de proteção", como a higiene regular das mãos e a procura precoce de cuidados médicos em centros de saúde.

observador.title: As notícias das 12h
observador.description: As notícias na Rádio Observador. Aconteça o que acontecer.

observador.title: Banco de Fomento terá aumento de capital de 1,5 mil milhões
observador.description: Atualmente, o capital do banco é de cerca de 500 milhões de euros e está previsto que a injeção de dinheiro seja progressiva, até o capital do banco totalizar dois mil milhões de euros em 2030.

observador.title: SATA reajusta operação após 175 voos afetados pelo nevoeiro
observador.description: SATA encontra-se a proceder a reajustes operacionais para "reacomodar os passageiros com a maior brevidade possível e minimizar os constrangimentos causados" pelas condições atmosféricas.

observador.title: Semana do Ambiente no Funchal promove limpeza de beatas
observador.description: Uma ação de limpeza de beatas em duas praças do Funchal assinala o arranque da Semana do Ambiente na capital madeirense, uma iniciativa promovida pela autarquia e que decorre até 6 de junho.

observador.title: As imagens da Lua azul em várias partes do mundo
observador.description: Expressão é utilizada para designar a segunda lua cheia num único mês. Tratou-se também de uma “microlua”, já que atingiu a fase um dia antes de alcançar o ponto mais distante da Terra na sua órbita.

observador.title: Seguro realça pobreza infantil e pede proteção da infância
observador.description: Para o Presidente da República o Dia Mundial da Criança é uma data de celebração, mas que deve, também, convocar à reflexão sobre o país que se constrói para as novas gerações.

observador.title: Teerão acusa EUA de violarem cessar fogo
observador.description: O porta-voz iraniano, Esmail Baghai, denunciou a violação de Israel no Líbano, criticando também o contínuo violar do cessar-fogo por parte dos EUA. "A nossa prioridade é acabar com a guerra".

observador.title: Governo de Israel ordenou bombardeamentos contra o Hezbollah
observador.description: Bombardeamentos contra o Hezbollah nos subúrbios do sul da capital libanesa têm como finalidade fragilizar um bastião do grupo terrorista, indica o ministro da Defesa, Israel Katz.

nzz.title: BILDSTRECKE - Der Krieg in der Ukraine: Die jüngsten Entwicklungen in Bildern
nzz.description: Die russische Invasion hat Millionen von Ukrainerinnen und Ukrainern in die Flucht getrieben. Während der Abnutzungskrieg unerbittlich weitergeht, droht Kiew durch die aussenpolitische Neuausrichtung von US-Präsident Donald Trump weiter unter Druck zu geraten. Die aktuellen Entwicklungen in Bildern.

nzz.title: Wenn das «Döp-dö-dö-dö-dö-dö-dö-dö-döö» ausbleibt: ein jähes Ende für das grosse Eishockey-Fest
nzz.description: Wie bei einem Steigerungslauf hat sich die Euphorie rund ums Schweizer Nationalteam während der Heim-WM aufgebaut. Die Niederlage im Final ist ein bitterer Schlusspunkt.

nzz.title: «Die Bevölkerung will Transparenz – Sie wollen verschleiern»: Schlagabtausch zwischen Mario Fehr und den Linken wegen Messerangriff von Winterthur
nzz.description: Im Zürcher Kantonsparlament haben die Parteien sehr unterschiedliche Schlüsse aus dem Vorfall gezogen. Jenes Thema, bei dem sich alle einig sind, verkam zur Fussnote.

nzz.title: Der von Intrigen zermürbte Urs Kessler tritt per sofort als Präsident von Swiss Ice Hockey zurück – sein Nachfolger soll Marc Lüthi werden
nzz.description: Wenige Stunden nach dem verlorenen WM-Final gegen Finnland gibt Kessler sein Amt ab.

nzz.title: LIVE-TICKER - Messerattacke in Winterthur: Mutmasslicher Täter sitzt in Untersuchungshaft
nzz.description: Ein Mann hat am Donnerstag drei Personen mit einer Stichwaffe verletzt. Er soll dabei «Allahu akbar» gerufen haben. Das sind die neusten Entwicklungen.

nzz.title: Vom Prügelknaben zum Dominator: der Aufstieg der Eishockey-Nation Schweiz
nzz.description: 1988 verlor das Schweizer Nationalteam noch gegen Amateure aus Alaska. Heute geht es in fast jedes Spiel als Favorit. Die Heim-WM endete mit einer Finalniederlage – und ist dennoch die Krönung eines Prozesses, der unter dem legendären Coach Ralph Krueger begann.

nzz.title: INTERAKTIV - So teuer ist Ihr Einkauf bei Aldi, Rewe und Co. geworden
nzz.description: Sie haben das Gefühl, alles wird teurer? Vergleichen Sie Ihren Kassenzettel von heute mit dem gleichen Einkauf von 2022 in deutschen Supermärkten – und erleben Sie Ihren persönlichen Preisschock.

nzz.title: DATENANALYSE - Wie beliebt ist Donald Trump?
nzz.description: Täglich aktualisierte Umfragewerte zeigen, wie die Amerikaner derzeit zur Amtsführung ihres Präsidenten stehen. Eine Übersicht in Grafiken.

nzz.title: ERKLÄRT - Zürcher Regierungsratswahlen: Martin Hübscher will definitiv für die SVP antreten
nzz.description: Im Regierungsrat werden mindestens vier Sitze frei. Die wichtigsten Fragen und Antworten zu den Wahlen 2027.

nzz.title: Silberne Tränen nach dem Gold-Spiel: War das der Schwanengesang der Spielergeneration um den Captain Roman Josi?
nzz.description: Zum dritten Mal in Serie verliert das Schweizer Eishockey-Nationalteam den WM-Final, ohne einen Treffer zu erzielen. War das der silberne Schlusspunkt in der Ära der goldenen Generation?

nzz.title: DIE NEUESTEN ENTWICKLUNGEN - Ebola-Ausbruch in Zentralafrika: Mehr als 1000 mutmassliche Verdachtsfälle in Ostkongo gemeldet
nzz.description: Die Weltgesundheitsorganisation hat den Gesundheitsnotstand ausgerufen. Es werden weitere Infizierte erwartet. Die wichtigsten Antworten zum Ebolavirus.

nzz.title: LIVE-TICKER - Iran-Krieg: Kuwait meldet feindliche Angriffe mit Raketen und Drohnen
nzz.description: Die USA und Israel haben Iran angegriffen. Teheran hat heftige Gegenangriffe lanciert. Gegenwärtig gilt eine Waffenruhe. Die Folgen des Konflikts sind weltweit spürbar. Die neuesten Entwicklungen im Live-Ticker.

nzz.title: KURZMELDUNGEN - Schweiz: In zwei Berner Gemeinden muss das Trinkwasser wegen Verschmutzung abgekocht werden
Bis zu 55 Tote bei Explosion in Myanmar
nzz.description: In einem Munitionslager in einem Rebellengebiet in Myanmar ist es zu einer verheerenden Explosion gekommen.

nzz.title: Referenzzinssatz bleibt bei 1,25 Prozent
nzz.description: Der hypothekarische Referenzzinssatz verharrt weiter auf dem Tiefstand. Mieterinnen und Mieter in der Schweiz können sich auf unveränderte Mietzinsen einstellen.

nzz.title: LIVE-TICKER - Krieg in der Ukraine: Frankreich stoppt Öltanker aus Russland im Atlantik +++ Viele Verletzte nach russischen Angriffen in der Ukraine
nzz.description: Seit über vier Jahren führt Russland Krieg gegen die Ukraine. Die wichtigsten Neuigkeiten im Überblick.

spiegel.title: Friedrich Merz vs. Hendrik Wüst: CDU-Spitze demonstriert Einigkeit beim Sauerland-Treffen
spiegel.description: Nach tagelang dräuenden Gerüchten über einen »Kanzlertausch« traf Friedrich Merz bei einem CDU-Treffen im Sauerland nun auf Hendrik Wüst.

spiegel.title: French Open: Tennisprofi Adolfo Daniel Vallejo muss nach »sexistischer Äußerung« 65.000 US-Dollar Geldstrafe zahlen
spiegel.description: Tennisprofi Adolfo Daniel Vallejo hat sich in Paris abfällig über die Schiedsrichterin Ana Carvalho geäußert. Die Turnierleitung greift nun durch: Für den Spruch muss er die Hälfte seines Preisgeldes abgeben.

spiegel.title: Nvidia: RTX-Spark-Chip soll Markt für Windows-Laptops aufmischen
spiegel.description: Der Chef persönlich übernahm die Präsentation: Nvidia will die Konkurrenz mit einem neuen Zentralprozessor unter Druck setzen, konzipiert für Rechner mit dem Betriebssystem Windows von Microsoft.

spiegel.title: Marilyn Monroe zum 100. Geburtstag: Bilder aus ihrem kurzen Leben
spiegel.description: Heute vor 100 Jahren kam in Los Angeles das Mädchen zur Welt, das als Marilyn Monroe zur Kino-Ikone wurde. Bilder aus einem kurzen, intensiven Leben.

spiegel.title: Hirnforschung: Eine Zelle, die »Kuchen« sagt
spiegel.description: Ein Bonner Neurowissenschaftler hat sich auf das rätselhafte Phänomen der Konzeptneuronen spezialisiert. Florian Mormann stößt tief ins Gehirn seiner Patienten vor – und gerät ins Schwärmen, wenn er von den Ergebnissen spricht.

spiegel.title: Nationalmannschaft: Deniz Undav trifft, beim DFB gibt es aber Bedenken
spiegel.description: Deniz Undav schießt Tore, legt auf und beherrscht die direkte Ansprache. Die Öffentlichkeit feiert den Unangepassten – beim DFB gibt es dennoch Restzweifel an ihm.

spiegel.title: Sydney: Zuschauer springt für Pianist bei »La La Land«-Aufführung ein
spiegel.description: Es ist wohl der Traum eines jeden kleinen Musikers: als Fan bei einem Konzert auf die Bühne gerufen werden. In Australien hat nun ein 21-Jähriger das Konzert seines Lebens gespielt.

spiegel.title: Dynamo Dresden: Zweitliga-Fußballer Lars Bünning nach Hirnblutung notoperiert
spiegel.description: Dresdens Innenverteidiger Lars Bünning musste nach einer Hirnblutung am Kopf operiert werden. Bünning ist ansprechbar, fällt jedoch auf unbestimmte Zeit aus.

spiegel.title: Abfall: Aufkommen in Deutschland fällt auf tiefsten Stand seit 2009
spiegel.description: Das Abfallaufkommen ist 2024 auf den niedrigsten Stand seit 2009 gesunken. Für die Umwelt mag das gut sein, die Zahlen weisen aber auch auf eine anhaltende Schwäche der Wirtschaft hin.

spiegel.title: 2G-Abschaltung: Warum sich Autofahrer auf das Mobilfunk-Aus vorbereiten müssen
spiegel.description: Für Neuwagen in der EU ist die sogenannte eCall-Funktion Pflicht: Bei schweren Unfällen wird darüber automatisch ein Notruf abgesetzt. Doch bald wird der Mobilfunkstandard 2G abgeschaltet. Was gilt dann?

spiegel.title: Iran: Zwei Männer nach landesweiten Protesten hingerichtet
spiegel.description: Iran hat zwei Männer im Kontext der landesweiten Proteste hingerichtet. Menschenrechtsorganisationen sprechen von einem Instrument der Einschüchterung und verweisen auf eine drastisch steigende Zahl von Exekutionen.

spiegel.title: Borussia Dortmund verpasst Aufstieg: Alexandra Popp landet in der Regionalliga
spiegel.description: Für Fußballstar Alexandra Popp geht es mit Borussia Dortmund vorerst nur in der dritten Liga weiter. Das BVB-Projekt »Bundesliga« könnte ins Stocken geraten – zumal Lokalrivale Schalke 04 für starke Konkurrenz sorgen wird.

spiegel.title: Bielefeld: Messerangreifer zu lebenslanger Haft verurteilt

phys-org.title: Nanoengineered materials can store and release hydrogen at room temperature
phys-org.description: Energy engineers worldwide are working on various new technologies that could help to limit greenhouse gas emissions on Earth and address climate change. One proposed alternative to polluting fossil fuels, such as petrol, diesel and natural gas, is hydrogen.

phys-org.title: A giant star may have destroyed itself in one of the universe's rarest explosions
phys-org.description: Astronomers may have discovered one of the clearest examples yet of a rare "pair-instability" supernova. It is a catastrophic explosion thought to completely destroy some of the most massive stars in the universe, leaving behind no remnant. The paper outlining the properties of this rare explosion was posted to the arXiv preprint server  on May 15.

phys-org.title: Student astronomer discovers 'Rosetta Stone' for mysterious cosmic signals
phys-org.description: An international team led by astronomers at the University of Sydney has uncovered the clearest evidence yet for the origin of an unusual class of cosmic signals. In doing so, they have identified a rare stellar system that is providing scientists with a natural laboratory to study extreme physics.

phys-org.title: 8 crested ibises released in Japan decades after extinction
phys-org.description: Eight crested ibises were released into the wild in a north-central Japanese town, decades after the birds went extinct in the country.

phys-org.title: Biopolymer-based hydrogel formulations for improved seed coating performance
phys-org.description: As climate change, soil degradation, and water scarcity place growing pressure on agriculture, scientists are looking for new ways to help crops germinate and grow more efficiently while reducing environmental impact. A new study involving researchers from Nazarbayev University's National Laboratory Astana published in Scientific Reports proposes a promising solution: biodegradable hydrogel coatings made from natural polymers.

phys-org.title: Record wildfire losses rocked 2025 even as global burned area neared all-time lows
phys-org.description: A new analysis of global wildfire activity in 2025 reveals the world experienced some of the most destructive and deadly fire events in recent history, despite the second lowest area burned since 2002. It highlights a continued trend toward fires becoming increasingly extreme, costly, and disastrous—both economically and in lives lost.

phys-org.title: Parasitic fly 'sacrifices sight' after finding host, study shows
phys-org.description: Deer keds—biting flies found across Europe, Asia, Africa and the Americas—use their eyes and flight to locate a host, typically deer, but occasionally humans or other mammals. Once they land, however, they shed their wings permanently and spend the rest of their lives crawling through fur and feeding on blood.

phys-org.title: A natural chemistry laboratory in protostar shock waves
phys-org.description: Life exists because elements combine to form complex organic molecules. Astrochemistry studies this process, trying to understand how nature creates carbon-based molecules critical for life. One source for these types of molecules is the outflows emitted by protostars.

phys-org.title: What 'biodegradable' packaging really means—and three key questions to ask about it
phys-org.description: "Biodegradable" has become one of the most reassuring words in modern packaging. It appears on coffee cups, shopping bags and food containers, implying a promise: this product is better for the environment because nature will eventually take care of it.

phys-org.title: Bacteria uncover distinct strategy to import rare sugar polymers, crystal structures show
phys-org.description: Even though sugars are often framed as simple sources of energy, they also serve as structurally complex and functionally diverse molecules that mediate interactions between organisms. Among these, β-1,2-glucans, which are a class of glucose-based polymers, stand out for their varied and sometimes subtle roles.

phys-org.title: Leaf forces help steer stomata as young plants grow, experiments reveal
phys-org.description: Scientists have uncovered how the interplay between cell shape and mechanical stress influences the orientation of stomata (microscopic pores on the leaf surface) during early plant development.

phys-org.title: Supermassive black holes could be the universe's biggest planet nurseries
phys-org.description: Supermassive black holes are the largest known black holes in the universe, sitting at the center of most large galaxies. They are sometimes described as cosmic monsters because they feed on surrounding gas and dust when they are active, as well as destroy anything that gets too close. But their reputation could be due for a rethink, as a new paper published on the arXiv preprint server suggests they may also be the birthplace of millions of planets.

phys-org.title: In Senegal, a 2,000‑year‑old iron workshop sheds new light on the past
phys-org.description: How was iron produced 2,000 years ago in Senegal? A recent study at the Didé West 1 archaeological site, in the Falémé Valley in eastern Senegal, sheds light on an ancient iron production technique.

phys-org.title: AI crosses catalyst boundaries to uncover new route for green hydrogen
phys-org.description: Discovering new catalysts is one of the central challenges in developing clean-energy technologies such as green hydrogen production. Yet catalyst discovery has traditionally remained confined within individual material families, limiting researchers' ability to transfer knowledge across chemically distinct systems.

phys-org.title: Legal reforms to stop abusive SLAPPs fail to stop chilling effect of the powerful, study warns
phys-org.description: Legal reforms designed to curb the abusive use of "SLAPPs" are insufficient to stop the rich and powerful trying to block freedom of speech, a new study warns. Measures in the U.S., U.K. and the EU to stop strategic lawsuits against public participation do not address the deep-seated inadequacies in the law which have a chilling effect on journalists and whistleblowers, the research says.

phys-org.title: A kohl bottle from York may hint at an ancient Egyptian in Roman-Britain
phys-org.description: Ancient Egyptians are often depicted wearing black eyeliner, known as kohl, which was stored in small containers. While kohl containers are typically found throughout Egypt and Sudan (Nubia), their presence beyond these areas is limited to only a handful of examples.

phys-org.title: Central Africa's wild meat dilemma: Why outright bans threaten food security for millions
phys-org.description: Millions of people in central Africa rely on wild meat for their nutrition, especially in rural areas around the Congo rainforest, the second largest tropical rainforest in the world. Here, meat from domestic animals is scarce due to poor national transport infrastructure, livestock diseases, and lack of forage. As a result, wild meat and freshwater fish are the main animal foods and provide the proteins and micro-nutrients needed for a healthy diet.

phys-org.title: Why many fungicide-treated soybean seeds may boost harvests but not farm profits
phys-org.description: Many soybean farmers use seeds treated with fungicides to ward off disease, but the profits from these increased yields might not offset the cost of the treatment in most cases, according to a study published in Scientific Reports by researchers at Penn State.

undark.title: A Peptide, a Secretive Scientist, and a Debate Over Evidence
undark.description: Access to unapproved peptides like BPC-157 has become a cause célèbre for the MAHA movement. Undark contributing editor Sara Talpos digs into the untold history of BPC-157 and its long journey from the scientific margins to the center of a debate over U.S. drug regulation.

undark.title: Book Review: Within Our Cells, the Miracle of Constant Mutation
undark.description: Our cells are constantly mutating in a battle for the survival of the fittest that is raging inside us daily, Roxanne Khamsi writes in “Beyond Inheritance.” Many of these mutations are harmless, others are cellular deviants that lead to disease, and remarkably, some can actually self-correct.

undark.title: The Six-Week Postpartum Checkup Comes Too Late
undark.description: In the U.S., maternity care generally ends with a checkup scheduled six weeks after giving birth. This single doctor’s appointment may be efficient for billing and discharge protocols, but the timing reflects the structure of the health care system more than the reality of maternal recovery.

undark.title: Book Review:  The Case for Making Data-Driven Decisions
undark.description: In “Beyond Belief: How Evidence Shows What Really Works,” science journalist Helen Pearson profiles a group of people working in medicine and other fields who became leaders of the worldwide evidence movement, which encourages the use of data from rigorous research to direct treatments, policies, and plans.

undark.title: What the Hantavirus Story Reveals About Medical Mistrust
undark.description: The reaction to an outbreak of hantavirus on a cruise ship reveals a story about mistrust in medicine and public health. In the U.S., hantavirus disproportionately kills Native Americans. A doctor who works at a hospital on Navajo Nation writes that such mistrust always lands hardest on the most vulnerable.

undark.title: Book Review: The Mind-Boggling Science of Enormous Numbers
undark.description: In “Huge Numbers: A Story of Counting Ambitiously, From 4½ to Fish 7,” mathematician Richard Elwes shows off his love of all things numeric, and, in particular, shines a spotlight on some of the largest numbers humans have ever contemplated, and the much larger numbers that await those who seek them out.

undark.title: When Scientific Arguments Obscure Moral Ones, Democracy Suffers
undark.description: The Pentagon’s new vaccine policy values individual choice over public health. Which of these values should be prioritized is a legitimate subject for democratic debate. But when experts respond to moral arguments animating policy decisions by reiterating facts, it undermines debate and fuels divisiveness.

undark.title: Book Review: The Life and Struggles of a Conservation Pioneer
undark.description: Over a career of many decades, George Schaller laid the groundwork for the field of conservation biology, and his pioneering research likely saved numerous species from extinction. In “Homesick for a World Unknown,” Miriam Horn documents his triumphs, challenges, and setbacks in meticulous detail.

undark.title: Medicine’s Move Toward Race-Neutral Risk Assessments
undark.description: Earlier this year, new guidelines were released for doctors assessing a patient’s risk for heart disease. The guidelines take a race-neutral and patient-informed approach that’s rooted in up-to-date science, one doctor writes, and offer a glimpse of a future in which health equity is the standard in medicine.

undark.title: In Coal Country, Black Lung Surges as Federal Protections Stall
undark.description: While the Trump administration is directing hundreds of millions of dollars to coal projects, miners in Appalachia are suffering from a resurgence of black lung disease. But industry pushback is delaying federal rules that would reduce miners’ exposure to deadly silica dust.

public-dom.title: Animal, Vegetable, Lamb: The Zoophyte from Tartary
public-dom.description: In the Middle Ages, rumours spread across Europe of a strange hybrid creature, half-animal, half-plant, known as the Vegetable Lamb of Tartary. A hoax based on fern rhizomes? A euphemism for culled fetal lambs? Or perhaps a medieval misapprehension of cotton? Thom Sliwowski traces the roots of this fabled zoophyte.

public-dom.title: Harold A. Taylor’s Autochromes of California Flowers (early 20th century)
public-dom.description: Photographs of flowers by an advocate of California’s beauty.

public-dom.title: The Prophecies of the Brahan Seer (1877)
public-dom.description: Historical predictions from the Scottish Nostradamus.

public-dom.title: “Plaything of the Gods”: Photographs of Pushball (early 1900s)
public-dom.description: Photographs and films of a forgotten pastime.

public-dom.title: Twilight of the Velocipede: Typesetting Races before the Age of Linotype
public-dom.description: Before Linotype revolutionised typesetting in the 1880s, compositors set texts by hand — and they set them *fast*. Alex Wright rediscovers the thrilling world of typesetting races, which drew crowds in the thousands, offered huge cash prizes, and helped women "Swifts" fight for workplace equity.

public-dom.title: Diagrams from Willem ten Rhijne’s De Acupunctura (1683)
public-dom.description: A Dutch physician’s encounter with acupuncture.

public-dom.title: Longitude by Way of Wounded Hounds: Kenelm Digby’s Sympathetick Powder (1669 edition)

proj-syn.title: Why Isn’t Europe Poorer Than the US?
proj-syn.description: Nobel laureate Paul Krugman has a point when he says that European living standards have largely kept pace with those in the US, despite flagging growth and innovation. But this will not remain true indefinitely: restoring Europe's ability to compete at the technological frontier remains essential to its future well-being.

proj-syn.title: The Real Choice Confronting Developing Countries
proj-syn.description: Lost in the debate about whether developing countries should pursue manufacturing- or services-led growth is the potential for new AI tools to make even informal workers far more productive. If governments can broaden access to such technologies, they no longer need to choose between strategies.

proj-syn.title: India’s Great Political Realignment
proj-syn.description: In recent years, the ruling Bharatiya Janata Party’s focus on religious identity, together with its “purification” of voter rolls, has created a more binary—and potentially volatile—political landscape, where elections increasingly reflect ethno-religious identity. This month’s elections in five states largely confirmed this trend.

proj-syn.title: Central Banking in an Age of Global Supply Shocks
proj-syn.description: The core assumptions underlying the decades-old inflation-targeting orthodoxy have proven to be unfit for a geopolitically fragmented world characterized by frequent supply-side disruptions. Under such conditions, central banks' traditional monetary policies are only as effective as markets believe them to be.

proj-syn.title: The Tech-MAGA Breakup Is Coming
proj-syn.description: Donald Trump has managed to fuse a backward-looking populist movement with a Silicon Valley vanguard whose guiding assumption is that AI will render a large share of ordinary people economically redundant. But with the tech billionaires now rewiring America's electricity grid and driving up costs, a split seems inevitable.

proj-syn.title: A Professor Should Work Hard and Grade Easy
proj-syn.description: The Harvard University faculty has now decided to limit the share of “A” grades given to students to about 20%. But, as the move's defenders freely admit, the intent is to increase professors' power and students' stress, not to generate excitement in the classroom.

proj-syn.title: What Price Hormuz?
proj-syn.description: Donald Trump has three primary objectives in the Persian Gulf: unwind the Iranian nuclear program, permanently reopen the Strait of Hormuz, and not be the president blamed for having “lost” Taiwan to China. The bad news for the US president is that he can achieve at most two of these goals.

proj-syn.title: The Mismeasurement of Europe’s Productivity
proj-syn.description: The Nobel laureate economist Paul Krugman uses the wrong metric—purchasing power parity—to make the case that Europe is not lagging far behind the US in terms of productivity. The right metric shows that the gap is growing.

proj-syn.title: Latin America’s Agricultural Boom Is Faltering
proj-syn.description: The productivity growth that transformed agriculture across Latin America and the Caribbean has slowed sharply in recent years, with farmers increasingly relying on costly inputs rather than efficiency gains. Without sustained public investment, the region risks losing competitiveness and reversing decades of hard-won progress.

proj-syn.title: Americans Can’t Afford Trump’s Economy
proj-syn.description: Prices are rising faster than wages in the US, and President Donald Trump’s policies are a key reason why. Now is the time for the Democratic Party to advance a credible and specific “affordability platform” that addresses the biggest culprits, from tariffs and energy prices to mass deportation of immigrants.

proj-syn.title: Britain’s Center Cannot Hold
proj-syn.description: A combination of globalization, deindustrialization, and other forces destroyed the old model of party politics that long prevailed in developed democracies. Nowhere is this more apparent than in the United Kingdom, where voters are angry and demanding radical solutions that no political leader can actually deliver.

proj-syn.title: Reading Between China’s Red Lines
proj-syn.description: Chinese President Xi Jinping’s blunt warning to US President Donald Trump about Taiwan was clearly intended to sharpen the distinction between this ultimatum and the many others Xi has issued. But expanding the number of non-negotiable positions reduces the space for effective diplomacy and raises the risk of accidental conflict.

proj-syn.title: The Pope Should Have Gone Further on AI
proj-syn.description: Pope Leo XIV has made waves with his first encyclical, in which he describes the development and deployment of new AI tools as a profound threat to human dignity. If anything, he has not gone far enough in pressing the question of what the technology is being designed to do.

proj-syn.title: China’s Long March to Technological Supremacy
proj-syn.description: China’s R&D prowess was visible in research output, patents, PhDs, and critical technologies for years, long before crystallizing into commercial products that Western investors, commentators, and policymakers noticed. And now it’s happening again.

proj-syn.title: The Pope’s Defense of Humanity
proj-syn.description: Pope Leo XIV is right to celebrate the grandeur of humanity, to criticize and reject posthumanism, and to emphasize the essential, categorical, and insurmountable difference between humans and machines. His first encyclical is a necessary exhortation to believers and non-believers alike.

proj-syn.title: India’s External Shock Is an Economic Opportunity
proj-syn.description: Despite strong fundamentals, India’s economy has major vulnerabilities stemming from its external account. With energy flows contested, shipping routes under threat, and capital markets increasingly shaped by geopolitics, the country must leverage its relative strength to weather current shocks and build long-term resilience.

proj-syn.title: The Economic Path to Climate Justice
proj-syn.description: Policymakers have used the concept of a “just transition” to make a morally and emotionally compelling case for decarbonization. But the experiences of Ethiopia, Pakistan, and South Africa show that rapid renewable-energy uptake in emerging and developing countries often comes down to affordability.

proj-syn.title: AI and Its Discontents
proj-syn.description: With AI hype reaching fever pitch, a backlash has begun, with university graduates, in particular, resisting a technology that could quickly render their skills obsolete. They are not alone in challenging AI boosters’ bubbly narrative. While the technology will transform the economy and upend labor markets, important bottlenecks and major risks will limit its productivity benefits—and the payoff for investors.
